scenario: A company needs a disaster recovery solution for their primary application in us-east-1 with an RTO of 15 minutes and RPO of 1 minute. They want to minimize costs during normal operations. Which TWO components should be part of their DR strategy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An Aurora Global Database with a secondary cluster in us-west-2 for sub-minute replication lag
Auto Scaling groups in us-west-2 configured to scale from zero when activated by Route 53 failover
A fully scaled duplicate environment running active-active in us-west-2
Manual AMI copies to us-west-2 performed weekly
Periodic database exports to S3 with cross-region replication

explanation: Aurora Global Database provides cross-region replication with less than 1 second lag (meeting RPO < 1 minute). A warm standby approach with ASGs that can rapidly scale up in the DR region meets the 15-minute RTO. This is more cost-effective than active-active while meeting the requirements. Weekly AMI copies and periodic exports don't meet the RPO.

scenario: A healthcare application must encrypt all data in transit between the client and the server, and encrypt all data at rest in S3. Which TWO configurations satisfy both requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure the ALB listener to use HTTPS with an ACM certificate for transit encryption
Enable SSE-KMS on the S3 bucket for at-rest encryption with audit capability
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed up encrypted uploads
Attach a security group to S3 to enforce encrypted connections
Use CloudFront signed URLs to enforce encrypted file downloads

explanation: HTTPS on the ALB (via ACM certificate) encrypts data in transit between client and server using TLS. SSE-KMS on S3 encrypts stored objects with KMS-managed keys and provides CloudTrail audit logs of key usage. Transfer Acceleration improves speed but doesn't provide encryption. S3 doesn't support security groups.

scenario: A news website serves millions of readers globally. Static assets (images, CSS, JavaScript) are stored in S3 and account for 80% of requests. Users in Asia and Europe report slow page load times. What should be implemented to reduce latency for all regions?

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Place an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket with edge caching
Deploy S3 buckets in each region and use Route 53 latency-based routing
Increase the S3 bucket's request rate by prefixing object keys with random characters

explanation: CloudFront caches content at 450+ edge locations worldwide, serving requests from the location nearest to the user. For static content, this dramatically reduces latency compared to fetching directly from S3 in a single region. Transfer Acceleration improves upload speed to S3, not download speed to end users.

scenario: A company runs EC2 instances that are significantly over-provisioned. CPU utilization averages 10-15% across the fleet. The operations team wants a data-driven approach to rightsize instances. Which AWS tool provides specific rightsizing recommendations?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch CPU utilization dashboards to manually assess instance sizing
AWS Compute Optimizer which analyzes utilization patterns and recommends optimal instance types
AWS Cost Explorer general spending reports
AWS Trusted Advisor basic checks for underutilized instances

explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze CloudWatch metrics (CPU, memory, network, disk) and recommends optimal EC2 instance types based on actual workload patterns. It provides specific recommendations like 'change from m5.2xlarge to m5.large' with projected savings. Trusted Advisor only flags instances below a threshold, without specific sizing recommendations.

scenario: A company has hundreds of Lambda functions connecting to an RDS MySQL database. During traffic spikes, the database reaches its maximum connection limit (1,000 connections) and new Lambda invocations fail. What is the recommended solution?

options.text: Increase the max_connections parameter on the RDS instance
Place Amazon RDS Proxy between Lambda and the database to pool connections
Use ElastiCache as a write-through cache to reduce database connections
Switch from RDS MySQL to DynamoDB to eliminate connection limits

explanation: RDS Proxy maintains a pool of established database connections that Lambda functions share. Instead of each Lambda invocation opening a new connection, RDS Proxy multiplexes thousands of concurrent Lambda connections into a smaller pool of database connections. This prevents connection exhaustion during traffic spikes.

scenario: An application performs the same 10 complex database queries repeatedly, with results changing only once per hour. The RDS PostgreSQL database is under heavy read load. What is the MOST effective way to reduce database load and improve response times?

options.text: Add RDS Read Replicas and distribute queries across them
Implement Amazon ElastiCache Redis to cache query results with a 1-hour TTL
Upgrade the RDS instance to a larger instance class
Enable RDS Performance Insights to identify and optimize slow queries

explanation: ElastiCache Redis caching eliminates redundant database queries by storing results in-memory with sub-millisecond latency. A 1-hour TTL matches the data refresh rate. Read Replicas help distribute load but still execute the same queries. Performance Insights helps identify bottlenecks but doesn't cache results.

scenario: A company runs an application in a single AWS region. They need to plan for a regional outage with an RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour while keeping DR costs minimal. Which DR strategy is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Multi-site active-active with full infrastructure in the DR region
Warm standby with scaled-down infrastructure running continuously in the DR region
Pilot light with core services (database replication) running and compute infrastructure ready to provision
Backup and restore with periodic snapshots copied to the DR region

explanation: Pilot light maintains only the critical core elements (like database replication) running in the DR region. Compute resources are pre-configured (AMIs, launch templates) but not running, keeping costs minimal. During failover, the infrastructure is provisioned and scaled up. This meets a 4-hour RTO and 1-hour RPO. Backup & restore has longer RTO; warm standby costs more.

scenario: A Lambda function in a private subnet needs to access an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database. The security team mandates that the database must not be accessible from the internet. How should this be configured?

options.text: Place RDS in a public subnet and restrict its security group to the Lambda CIDR
Deploy the Lambda function inside the VPC private subnet and configure its security group to allow traffic to the RDS security group
Use RDS Proxy with a public endpoint and IAM authentication
Connect Lambda to RDS using an internet gateway with restrictive NACLs

explanation: Lambda can be configured to run inside a VPC, connecting to private resources. The Lambda function's security group must allow outbound traffic to the RDS port, and the RDS security group must allow inbound from Lambda's security group. Both resources stay in private subnets, ensuring no internet exposure.

scenario: A data analytics team runs Apache Spark jobs that require high-throughput sequential reads of large files (50GB+). The jobs are throughput-sensitive, not IOPS-sensitive. Which EBS volume type offers the best price-performance for this workload?

options.text: gp3 (General Purpose SSD) for balanced performance
io2 Block Express for maximum IOPS
st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) for high-throughput sequential workloads
sc1 (Cold HDD) for the lowest storage cost

explanation: st1 volumes are designed for large sequential workloads like data warehousing, log processing, and big data analytics. They deliver up to 500 MB/s throughput at a lower cost than SSD volumes. gp3 and io2 are optimized for random IOPS. sc1 has lower throughput and is designed for infrequently accessed data.

scenario: A content delivery architecture serves dynamic API responses and static assets. The team wants to optimize performance by caching static assets at the edge while ensuring dynamic API requests always reach the origin. Which TWO CloudFront configurations achieve this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure cache behaviors with long TTL for static asset paths (/static/*, /images/*)
Set the default cache behavior to forward all headers for dynamic API paths, disabling caching
Enable Origin Shield to reduce load on the origin server
Use signed URLs for all content to prevent unauthorized caching
Enable field-level encryption for all cached responses

explanation: CloudFront cache behaviors allow different caching rules per URL path pattern. Static asset paths get long TTLs for edge caching, while dynamic API paths forward all headers (which effectively disables caching since each unique header set creates a different cache key). This gives you edge performance for static content and fresh responses for dynamic requests.

scenario: A media company stores video assets in S3 and needs them replicated to a different region for disaster recovery. Only new objects uploaded after enabling replication should be replicated. What should they configure?

options.text: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with versioning enabled on both buckets
Copy all existing objects using aws s3 sync and set up CloudWatch Events for new objects
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration between the two regions
Configure S3 Batch Operations to periodically copy objects between buckets

explanation: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) automatically replicates new objects to a destination bucket in another region. Versioning must be enabled on both source and destination buckets. By default, CRR only replicates new objects after the rule is created. Existing objects can be replicated using S3 Batch Replication if needed.

scenario: A company needs to ensure their web application automatically recovers from instance failures and maintains at least 4 healthy instances across 3 AZs at all times. Which TWO configurations are required? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An Auto Scaling group with min=4 spanning 3 AZs with ELB health checks
ALB target group health checks with a custom health check path on the application
CloudWatch alarm to send an email notification when instances fail
A launch template specifying a single specific Availability Zone
Enhanced monitoring enabled on all EC2 instances

explanation: Auto Scaling group with min=4 across 3 AZs automatically replaces unhealthy instances and distributes them across zones. ELB health checks (instead of default EC2 health checks) detect application-level failures, not just instance hardware issues. The custom health check path validates that the application is truly functional, not just that the instance is running.

scenario: A stateful web application stores user session data in memory on EC2 instances. When Auto Scaling terminates an instance, users lose their session. How should the architecture be modified to maintain session persistence?

options.text: Enable sticky sessions on the ALB to always route users to the same instance
Externalize session storage to Amazon ElastiCache Redis for shared, persistent sessions
Increase the instance size to handle more sessions without scaling
Store session data in EBS volumes and reattach them to new instances

explanation: Externalizing sessions to ElastiCache Redis makes the application tier truly stateless, allowing any instance to serve any user. Redis provides sub-millisecond access and supports replication for high availability. Sticky sessions create uneven load distribution and sessions are still lost if the sticky instance fails.

scenario: A batch video transcoding pipeline can tolerate interruptions and automatically retry failed jobs. Individual jobs take 10-30 minutes. The company wants to minimize compute costs. Which EC2 purchasing option should they use?

options.text: On-Demand Instances for reliability and availability
Spot Instances with checkpointing for up to 90% cost savings
Reserved Instances with a 1-year term
Dedicated Instances for consistent performance

explanation: Spot Instances provide up to 90% discount over On-Demand and are ideal for fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads like batch processing and video transcoding. With short job durations (10-30 min) and automatic retry, the impact of Spot interruptions is minimal. Checkpointing ensures no work is lost if an instance is reclaimed.

scenario: Users uploading large video files (2-10GB) from South America to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 experience very slow upload speeds due to geographic distance. What is the MOST effective way to accelerate these uploads?

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket to route uploads through CloudFront edge locations
Increase the S3 bucket's provisioned throughput capacity
Create a VPN connection between South America and the us-east-1 region
Use S3 multipart upload with larger part sizes to improve throughput

explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations to accelerate uploads. Data is ingested at the nearest edge location and transferred to S3 over AWS's optimized backbone network, significantly improving speed for long-distance transfers. Multipart upload enables parallel upload of parts but doesn't address network path optimization.

scenario: An event-driven architecture uses multiple AWS services. The team needs to route different types of events (user signups, order completions, inventory updates) from various sources to specific targets based on event content. Which service provides content-based routing of events?

options.text: Amazon SNS with message filtering policies
Amazon EventBridge with event rules and patterns
Amazon SQS with multiple queues
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with partition keys

explanation: Amazon EventBridge provides content-based routing through event rules with pattern matching. Rules can match on any field in the event JSON structure and route to specific targets (Lambda, SQS, Step Functions, etc.). SNS message filtering is simpler and limited to message attributes, not body content. EventBridge is the preferred service for event-driven architectures.

scenario: A machine learning team needs a high-performance shared file system for training jobs running on a cluster of EC2 GPU instances. The workload requires sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s throughput for reading training data from S3. Which storage solution is BEST?

options.text: Amazon EFS with Provisioned Throughput mode
Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 training data bucket
An NFS server running on a large EC2 instance with instance store volumes
Amazon S3 with multipart download optimization

explanation: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system designed for compute-intensive workloads like ML training. It integrates natively with S3, lazily loading data as needed. It provides sub-millisecond latencies and hundreds of GB/s throughput. EFS is POSIX-compliant but doesn't match Lustre's HPC-grade throughput.

scenario: A security team needs to continuously detect unauthorized activity and automatically remediate compliance violations across their AWS environment. Which TWO services working together provide this capability? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty for intelligent threat detection
AWS Config rules with automatic remediation actions via SSM
Amazon Inspector for EC2 vulnerability assessments
AWS Artifact for compliance report downloads
AWS Trusted Advisor for cost optimization checks

explanation: GuardDuty uses ML and threat intelligence to detect unauthorized behavior like unusual API calls, cryptocurrency mining, or compromised credentials. AWS Config rules continuously evaluate resource compliance and can trigger automatic remediation through SSM Automation documents.

scenario: A development team has unpredictable S3 access patterns — some objects are accessed frequently for a few days, then not at all for months, with no predictable schedule. They want to minimize storage costs without managing lifecycle rules. Which storage class is BEST?

options.text: S3 Standard for consistent performance
S3 One Zone-IA for reduced redundancy at lower cost
S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization based on access patterns
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for infrequent access with fast retrieval

explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on actual usage patterns. Frequently accessed objects stay in the Frequent Access tier, and objects not accessed for 30+ days move to Infrequent Access (40% savings), then to Archive (68% savings) after 90 days. There are no retrieval fees or lifecycle management needed.

scenario: An application processes messages from SQS but occasionally fails during processing. Messages that fail 3 times should be moved to a separate queue for investigation rather than being retried indefinitely. What should be configured?

options.text: Set the message retention period to 3 minutes
Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) with a maximum receive count of 3
Enable long polling with a 3-second timeout
Set the visibility timeout to 3 seconds to force rapid retries

explanation: A dead-letter queue (DLQ) with maxReceiveCount=3 automatically moves messages that have been received (and not deleted) 3 times to the DLQ. This prevents poison messages from blocking the queue and preserves them for debugging. The visibility timeout controls how long a message is invisible after being read, not retry behavior.

scenario: A company runs a web application on EC2 instances that have steady, predictable usage 24/7 for the next 3 years. They are currently using On-Demand instances and want to reduce compute costs significantly. Which purchasing option offers the GREATEST savings?

options.text: Spot Instances for up to 90% discount
3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for up to 72% discount compared to On-Demand
EC2 Savings Plans with no upfront payment
Dedicated Hosts with reserved pricing

explanation: For steady, predictable 24/7 workloads with a known 3-year commitment, All Upfront Reserved Instances provide the deepest discount (up to 72% vs On-Demand). Spot Instances can be interrupted and aren't suitable for always-on production. Savings Plans offer flexibility but slightly lower maximum discount. Dedicated Hosts are for licensing or compliance, not cost optimization.

scenario: A company runs a TCP-based gaming server that must serve players globally with the lowest possible latency. The server runs on EC2 instances in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. DNS-based routing adds latency due to DNS resolution times. What should be used instead?

options.text: Route 53 with latency-based routing policy
AWS Global Accelerator with endpoints in both regions
CloudFront with custom origin configurations
A Network Load Balancer with cross-region target groups

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator uses Anycast IP addresses that route traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal regional endpoint. Unlike DNS-based routing, it doesn't depend on DNS resolution or TTL caching. It provides deterministic routing and improves TCP performance by up to 60% compared to the public internet. CloudFront is for HTTP/HTTPS content, not arbitrary TCP.

scenario: A company wants to archive 500TB of compliance data that will never be accessed under normal circumstances but must be retrievable within 12 hours for regulatory audits. What is the MOST cost-effective storage option?

options.text: S3 Standard-IA for infrequent access at reduced cost
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval with standard retrieval (3-5 hours)
S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval (within 12 hours) at the lowest cost
Amazon EFS with Infrequent Access storage class

explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class in AWS, designed for long-term data archiving. At ~$1/TB/month, it costs about 95% less than S3 Standard. Standard retrieval takes up to 12 hours, which meets the requirement. Glacier Flexible Retrieval costs more (~$3.60/TB/month). For pure archival with 12-hour retrieval tolerance, Deep Archive is optimal.

scenario: A company is migrating workloads to AWS and wants flexible compute savings without committing to specific instance types or regions. They need at least a 1-year commitment. Which purchasing option provides the BEST flexibility with meaningful savings?

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances for specific instance types in specific regions
Compute Savings Plans for flexible savings across instance families, sizes, and regions
Convertible Reserved Instances that can be exchanged for different types
Spot Instances for the highest possible discount

explanation: Compute Savings Plans offer up to 66% savings with maximum flexibility — they apply to any EC2 instance family, size, OS, tenancy, and region, as well as Fargate and Lambda usage. Standard RIs are locked to specific instance type and region. Convertible RIs offer flexibility but lower discount. Spot Instances can't guarantee availability.

scenario: An organization with 50 AWS accounts needs to enforce a policy preventing any account from launching EC2 instances outside of eu-west-1 and us-east-1. What is the MOST scalable approach?

options.text: Create an IAM policy in each account denying ec2:RunInstances outside the allowed regions
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations restricting ec2:RunInstances to the two regions
Use AWS Config rules to detect and terminate non-compliant instances
Configure VPC settings in each account to only allow resources in approved regions

explanation: SCPs in AWS Organizations provide centralized, preventive guardrails that apply across all member accounts. They cannot be overridden by account-level IAM policies. IAM policies per account don't scale and can be modified by account admins. Config rules are detective, not preventive.

scenario: A company wants to allow developers to create any IAM resource but prevent them from escalating their own privileges beyond a defined boundary. Which TWO mechanisms should be used together? (Select TWO.)

options.text: IAM permissions boundaries to set the maximum permissions developers can grant
An SCP requiring that all created roles include the permissions boundary
AWS CloudTrail to log all IAM API calls for post-event review
IAM Access Analyzer to detect overly permissive policies
Amazon Detective to investigate privilege escalation patterns

explanation: Permissions boundaries define the maximum permissions an IAM entity can have, regardless of identity-based policies. The SCP ensures that any role or user created by developers must attach the boundary, preventing them from creating entities with broader permissions than allowed.

scenario: An organization's S3 buckets have been accidentally made public multiple times. Management wants a preventive control that ensures no bucket across the entire organization can ever be made public. What is the BEST approach?

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie on all accounts to detect public bucket access
Apply an SCP denying s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with Block Public Access always ON, plus enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level for all accounts
Use AWS Config auto-remediation to flip buckets back to private after detection
Create an EventBridge rule to detect PutBucketPolicy calls and invoke Lambda to revert them

explanation: Enabling S3 Block Public Access at the account level prevents any bucket in that account from being made public. An SCP ensures account administrators cannot disable this setting. This is a preventive control. Config remediation and EventBridge rules are detective/reactive approaches that leave a window of exposure.

scenario: A company's VPC generates 5TB of monthly data transfer charges from EC2 instances accessing S3 through a NAT Gateway. How can they eliminate this cost while maintaining private connectivity to S3?

options.text: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to reduce data transfer costs
Replace the NAT Gateway with a cheaper NAT Instance
Create an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint which is free and eliminates NAT Gateway charges for S3 traffic
Move the EC2 instances to a public subnet and access S3 directly via the internet

explanation: S3 Gateway VPC Endpoints are free — no hourly charge and no data processing charge. S3 traffic routed through the endpoint bypasses the NAT Gateway entirely, eliminating both the NAT Gateway data processing charge ($0.045/GB) and the Gateway hourly charge for that traffic. This saves $225/month on 5TB of S3 traffic alone.

scenario: A data warehouse team needs to run complex analytical SQL queries across petabytes of structured data with fast query performance and the ability to scale compute independently of storage. Which AWS service is BEST suited?

options.text: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL with read replicas for parallel query execution
Amazon Redshift with RA3 nodes for managed columnar storage with independent compute scaling
Amazon Athena for serverless queries directly on S3 data
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with parallel query enabled

explanation: Amazon Redshift is purpose-built for data warehousing with columnar storage, massively parallel processing (MPP), and result caching. RA3 nodes separate compute and storage, allowing independent scaling. Athena is serverless SQL on S3 but is optimized for ad-hoc queries, not sustained complex analytics. Aurora is OLTP, not OLAP.

scenario: A VPC hosts a private application that must call AWS services (CloudWatch, SNS) without any internet access. The company wants to minimize data transfer costs. What should be implemented?

options.text: Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet to allow outbound internet access
Create VPC interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for CloudWatch and SNS
Set up a VPN connection to route AWS API traffic through the corporate data center
Peer the VPC with the default VPC which has internet access

explanation: VPC interface endpoints (PrivateLink) create private connections to AWS services within the VPC, eliminating the need for internet access via NAT Gateway. This also reduces data transfer costs since PrivateLink traffic stays on the AWS network. NAT Gateway charges per GB processed.

scenario: A company has multiple development and testing environments that engineers use only during business hours (8 AM to 6 PM, Monday-Friday). The environments run on EC2 instances and RDS databases. What is the MOST cost-effective approach?

options.text: Use smaller instance types and accept slower performance during off-hours
Implement scheduled scaling with AWS Instance Scheduler to stop instances outside business hours
Migrate all dev/test to Spot Instances that auto-terminate
Use Reserved Instances for all dev/test environments to get discounts

explanation: AWS Instance Scheduler automates starting and stopping EC2 and RDS instances on a schedule. Stopping dev/test resources outside business hours (14 hours/day weekdays + weekends) reduces compute costs by approximately 70%. Stopped instances incur no compute charges (only EBS storage). Reserved Instances for intermittent use waste money during off-hours.

scenario: An application running on Amazon EC2 must read objects from an S3 bucket and write messages to an SQS queue. The security team requires that no long-term credentials be stored on the instances. What is the MOST secure solution?

options.text: Store IAM user access keys in an encrypted file on the instance
Attach an IAM role with an instance profile granting least-privilege S3 and SQS permissions
Use the root account credentials via environment variables
Generate temporary keys manually using the AWS CLI and store them in Parameter Store

explanation: IAM instance profiles provide temporary, automatically-rotated credentials to EC2 via the instance metadata service. This eliminates long-term credential management. Using access keys—even encrypted—introduces secret management overhead and security risk.

scenario: A development team needs to share an encrypted AMI from Account A with Account B. The AMI is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What additional step is required beyond sharing the AMI?

options.text: Re-encrypt the AMI using the default AWS managed key before sharing
Update the KMS key policy in Account A to grant Account B permission to use the key
Copy the AMI to Account B as an unencrypted AMI
Create an identical KMS key in Account B with the same key material

explanation: When sharing an encrypted AMI cross-account, the KMS key policy must explicitly grant the target account permissions (kms:DescribeKey, kms:CreateGrant, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt). Without this, Account B cannot decrypt the AMI's backing EBS snapshots during instance launch.

scenario: A company needs to discover and classify sensitive data like credit card numbers and personal information stored across hundreds of S3 buckets. Which service should they use?

options.text: AWS Inspector to scan S3 objects for vulnerabilities
Amazon Macie to automatically discover and classify sensitive data in S3
AWS Config to evaluate S3 bucket configurations
Amazon Comprehend to perform NLP analysis on stored documents

explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify, and protect sensitive data (PII, financial data, credentials) stored in Amazon S3. Inspector scans EC2 and container vulnerabilities, not S3 data content. Config evaluates resource configuration compliance, not data content.

scenario: A company wants to restrict access to an S3 bucket so that only resources within a specific VPC can reach it, without routing traffic through the internet. Which combination of actions achieves this?

options.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint and add a bucket policy with aws:SourceVpc condition
Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and add a bucket policy with aws:sourceVpce condition
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and restrict access to the VPC CIDR range
Configure a NAT Gateway and add a bucket policy restricting to the NAT's Elastic IP

explanation: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint provides private connectivity to S3 without an internet gateway or NAT. The bucket policy's aws:sourceVpce condition restricts access to traffic originating from the specific VPC endpoint, ensuring private-only access.

scenario: A team is running an application that stores user-uploaded files in Amazon EFS. They need the file system to automatically scale storage capacity and throughput based on usage without provisioning in advance. Which EFS throughput mode should they choose?

options.text: EFS Provisioned Throughput mode with a fixed throughput setting
EFS Bursting Throughput mode which scales with stored data size
EFS Elastic Throughput mode which automatically scales throughput independently of storage
EFS Max I/O performance mode for maximum aggregate throughput

explanation: EFS Elastic Throughput mode automatically scales throughput up or down based on workload demands, independent of file system size. You pay only for the throughput consumed. Bursting mode scales throughput proportionally to storage size, which may not meet needs for small but throughput-intensive workloads. Max I/O is a performance mode, not a throughput mode.

scenario: A company needs to build a real-time dashboard that processes and visualizes clickstream data from their website. The data arrives at 100,000 events per second during peak hours. Which TWO services should form the core of the data ingestion and processing pipeline? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for real-time data ingestion at scale
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (Kinesis Data Analytics) for real-time stream processing
Amazon SQS Standard queue for buffering clickstream events
AWS Batch for processing large volumes of event data
Amazon S3 with event notifications for processing uploaded files

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams handles real-time ingestion of high-volume streaming data (up to millions of records per second). Managed Apache Flink processes the stream in real-time with SQL or Java/Python applications for windowed aggregations, filtering, and enrichment. SQS is message-oriented, not optimized for streaming analytics. AWS Batch is for batch processing.

scenario: A company must ensure that every AWS API call across all regions and accounts is logged and stored immutably for 7 years to meet regulatory requirements. What is the MOST effective approach?

options.text: Enable CloudTrail in each account individually and store logs in local S3 buckets
Create an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail that logs all accounts to a centralized S3 bucket with Object Lock
Enable VPC Flow Logs across all VPCs and store in CloudWatch Logs
Use AWS Config to record all API-related configuration changes

explanation: An organization trail in CloudTrail automatically captures API calls across all AWS accounts in the organization. Storing logs in an S3 bucket with Object Lock (compliance mode) ensures immutability. VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic, not API calls. Config records resource state changes, not all API calls.

scenario: A three-tier web application must maintain availability even if an entire Availability Zone fails. The application tier is stateless. Which architecture provides this resilience?

options.text: Deploy all tiers in a single AZ with automated EBS snapshots for recovery
Deploy an ALB across multiple AZs with Auto Scaling groups spanning at least two AZs
Use a single large EC2 instance with enhanced networking for fast recovery
Deploy in a single AZ and use Route 53 health checks to redirect traffic

explanation: An ALB distributes traffic across instances in multiple AZs. Auto Scaling ensures the desired capacity is maintained even if one AZ fails by launching replacement instances in healthy AZs. This provides active-active resilience with no manual intervention. Single-AZ deployments are single points of failure.

scenario: A microservices architecture has a frontend API that receives bursts of 50,000 requests per second during flash sales. The backend order processing service can only handle 5,000 requests per second. How should the architecture be designed to avoid dropping orders?

options.text: Scale the frontend to match the backend's processing rate using throttling
Place an Amazon SQS queue between the frontend and backend to buffer requests
Deploy the backend on larger EC2 instances to match the frontend throughput
Use Amazon ElastiCache to temporarily store orders and replay them later

explanation: SQS decouples the fast producer (frontend) from the slow consumer (backend) by buffering messages durably. The backend processes messages at its own pace from the queue. This is the standard pattern for handling traffic spikes without losing data. ElastiCache is a cache, not a durable message buffer.

scenario: An application needs to call APIs in a partner's AWS account. The partner provides an IAM role ARN with an external ID. How should the application securely obtain credentials to access the partner's resources?

options.text: Request the partner to create IAM user credentials and embed them in the application
Use AWS STS AssumeRole with the partner's role ARN and the provided external ID
Configure VPC peering between both accounts for direct network access
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share resources directly

explanation: STS AssumeRole enables secure cross-account access by exchanging the calling identity for temporary credentials scoped to the partner's role. The external ID prevents the 'confused deputy' problem by ensuring only authorized callers can assume the role. This avoids long-term credential sharing.

scenario: A team needs to query and analyze data stored in S3 in Parquet format using standard SQL without setting up any infrastructure. They run ad-hoc queries a few times per week. Which service provides the most cost-effective solution?

options.text: Amazon EMR with Hive for SQL-on-Hadoop queries
Amazon Athena for serverless, pay-per-query SQL on S3
Load the data into Amazon Redshift for optimized query performance
Use Amazon RDS with the S3 import feature to load data for querying

explanation: Amazon Athena is serverless — no infrastructure to manage — and charges only per TB of data scanned. It works directly on S3 data in formats like Parquet, ORC, CSV, and JSON. Parquet's columnar format works especially well with Athena since it enables column pruning to reduce scanned data. For infrequent queries, pay-per-query is far more cost-effective than provisioned services.

scenario: A company runs compute workloads that aren't performance-sensitive but run 24/7. They want to reduce costs by switching from x86 (Intel/AMD) instances to a more cost-effective processor architecture. Which EC2 instance family should they evaluate?

options.text: T3 burstable instances for lower baseline costs
Graviton-based instances (M7g, C7g, R7g) for up to 40% better price-performance than x86
Mac instances for Apple Silicon efficiency
Inf2 instances optimized for inference workloads

explanation: AWS Graviton processors (ARM-based, custom-designed by AWS) offer up to 40% better price-performance compared to equivalent x86 instances. Graviton instances (identifiable by the 'g' suffix: m7g, c7g, r7g) are ideal for general-purpose, compute-intensive, and memory-intensive workloads. Most Linux-based applications run without modification on ARM.

scenario: A web application faces frequent SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. The company also needs protection against large-scale volumetric DDoS attacks targeting their Application Load Balancer. Which TWO services should be combined? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AWS WAF with managed rule groups for SQL injection and XSS
AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS protection with cost protection
Amazon Inspector for vulnerability scanning
Amazon Macie for data classification
AWS Firewall Manager for cross-account rule management

explanation: AWS WAF protects against application-layer attacks (SQLi, XSS) using managed and custom rule groups. Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection for ALB, CloudFront, and Route 53, including 24/7 DRT support and cost protection during attacks.

scenario: A company has a regulatory requirement that encryption keys must never leave a hardware security module and must be under their exclusive control. They need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated key storage. Which service meets this requirement?

options.text: AWS KMS with customer managed keys
AWS CloudHSM providing dedicated single-tenant HSM instances
AWS Secrets Manager with encryption enabled
Server-side encryption with S3-managed keys (SSE-S3)

explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules. Keys never leave the HSM boundary and the customer has exclusive control. KMS uses shared multi-tenant HSMs (FIPS 140-2 Level 2) where AWS manages the HSM infrastructure.

scenario: A notification system must send a single event to multiple subscribers — an SQS queue for order processing, a Lambda function for analytics, and an HTTPS endpoint for a partner webhook — simultaneously. Which pattern should be used?

options.text: Publish the event to multiple SQS queues using separate API calls from the application
Use an SNS topic with SQS, Lambda, and HTTPS subscriptions for fan-out
Create a Kinesis Data Stream with multiple consumers
Use EventBridge with a single rule targeting all three destinations

explanation: SNS fan-out is the standard pattern for broadcasting a single message to multiple subscribers of different types. An SNS topic can have SQS, Lambda, HTTP/S, email, and SMS subscriptions simultaneously. Each subscriber receives a copy of every message independently. This decouples the publisher from subscribers.

scenario: A financial trading platform requires the lowest possible network latency between EC2 instances in a cluster that perform high-frequency inter-node communication. Which EC2 placement strategy should be used?

options.text: Spread placement group to maximize hardware isolation
Partition placement group to reduce correlated failures
Cluster placement group to pack instances physically close together
Default placement to let AWS optimize for availability

explanation: Cluster placement groups place instances in a single Availability Zone on the same underlying hardware rack, providing the lowest network latency and highest network throughput between instances (up to 100 Gbps with enhanced networking). Spread groups maximize isolation. Partition groups reduce correlated failures for distributed systems like HDFS/Kafka.

scenario: A company needs to perform a blue/green deployment of their application with the ability to instantly switch traffic from the old version to the new version, and roll back within seconds if issues arise. Which approach is BEST?

options.text: Deploy the new version on separate instances behind a second ALB and use Route 53 weighted routing to shift traffic
Use an ALB with two target groups and swap the listener rule to point to the new target group
Perform a rolling update by replacing instances one at a time in the Auto Scaling group
Use CloudFormation stack updates with UpdatePolicy to replace the entire stack

explanation: ALB listener rule swapping enables instant blue/green switching. Both old (blue) and new (green) target groups run simultaneously. The ALB listener rule is updated to forward traffic to the green group. Rollback is instant by reverting the listener rule. Route 53 weighted routing introduces DNS TTL delays.

scenario: A company needs to protect their RDS database against accidental deletion by an administrator while still allowing normal stop/start/modify operations. Which feature should be enabled?

options.text: Enable RDS automated backups with 35-day retention
Enable RDS deletion protection
Create a read replica to serve as a backup in case of deletion
Take manual snapshots before any administrative operation

explanation: RDS deletion protection prevents the database instance from being deleted through the console, CLI, or API. An administrator must first disable deletion protection before deleting the instance, providing a two-step safeguard against accidental deletion. Automated backups and snapshots help with data recovery but don't prevent the deletion itself.

scenario: A global SaaS company needs their DynamoDB data to be available with single-digit millisecond read latency in US, Europe, and Asia simultaneously, with active write capability in each region. Which feature should they use?

options.text: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda-based cross-region replication
DynamoDB Global Tables for multi-region, multi-active replication
DynamoDB DAX clusters deployed in each region reading from a single-region table
DynamoDB on-demand backup and restore across regions

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables provide fully managed multi-region, multi-active replication. Applications can read and write to local table replicas with single-digit millisecond latency. Changes are automatically propagated to all replicas. DAX is a read-through cache for a single table, not cross-region replication.

scenario: A company needs to issue free SSL/TLS certificates for their public-facing Application Load Balancer and automatically renew them. Which service should they use?

options.text: Purchase certificates from a third-party CA and manually install them on the ALB
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision and manage public certificates
Generate self-signed certificates using OpenSSL and upload to IAM
Use AWS Private CA to issue public-facing certificates

explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provides free public SSL/TLS certificates that integrate directly with ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. ACM handles automatic renewal. AWS Private CA is for internal/private certificates and incurs charges. Self-signed certificates cause browser warnings.

scenario: A company stores sensitive customer PII in Amazon S3. A compliance audit requires that all objects be encrypted using keys the company fully controls, with the ability to audit key usage. Which approach meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable SSE-S3 default encryption on the bucket
Enable SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) and enable CloudTrail key-level logging
Encrypt objects client-side using application-level AES and upload via HTTPS
Use S3 Bucket Key with an AWS managed key to reduce KMS costs

explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed CMK gives the company full control over key policies, rotation, and grants. CloudTrail logs every Encrypt/Decrypt API call for auditing. SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys without customer control. Client-side encryption works but doesn't leverage AWS-native key audit trails.

scenario: A serverless application uses Lambda functions triggered by API Gateway. Some Lambda functions occasionally time out when connecting to a downstream RDS database due to connection pool exhaustion. What should be implemented to resolve this?

options.text: Increase the Lambda function timeout to 15 minutes
Use Amazon RDS Proxy to pool and manage database connections
Increase the RDS instance size to support more connections
Cache all database responses in Lambda's /tmp directory

explanation: RDS Proxy manages a pool of database connections, allowing Lambda functions to share connections efficiently. Without RDS Proxy, each Lambda invocation opens a new database connection, quickly exhausting the connection limit under high concurrency. RDS Proxy also handles failover transparently.

scenario: An e-commerce platform needs full-text search across millions of product listings with faceted filtering, fuzzy matching, and auto-suggestions. The search must return results within 100ms. Which AWS service should be used?

options.text: DynamoDB with scan operations and filter expressions
Amazon OpenSearch Service with relevant index mappings and search templates
Amazon RDS with PostgreSQL full-text search indexes
Amazon CloudSearch for managed search domains

explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service (successor to Elasticsearch Service) is purpose-built for full-text search, log analytics, and real-time monitoring. It supports fuzzy matching, faceted search, autocomplete suggestions, and relevance tuning. DynamoDB Scan operations are expensive and slow for full-text search. RDS full-text search doesn't scale as well for complex search requirements.

scenario: A media company stores user-uploaded videos in S3. They want to minimize costs by: (1) serving videos efficiently to global viewers and (2) automatically archiving videos not viewed for 90 days. Which TWO solutions address both requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: CloudFront CDN to cache and serve videos from edge locations, reducing S3 transfer costs
S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days of no access
S3 Requester Pays bucket so viewers pay for data transfer
Enable S3 Object Lock to prevent costly accidental deletions
Compress all videos with H.265 codec before uploading to reduce storage size

explanation: CloudFront reduces costs by caching videos at edge locations — S3 transfer to CloudFront is free, and CloudFront-to-viewer transfer is cheaper than direct S3 transfer. S3 Lifecycle rules with the 'days since last access' filter automatically transition unwatched videos to Glacier, reducing storage costs by ~68%. Together these address both serving efficiency and archival.

scenario: A company is building a mobile application that requires user sign-up, sign-in, and social login through Google and Facebook. User data must be stored in DynamoDB with per-user access control. Which service should be used?

options.text: IAM users with programmatic access for each mobile user
Amazon Cognito User Pools for authentication and Identity Pools for authorized AWS access
AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) with SAML federation
AWS STS AssumeRole with a custom-built token vending machine

explanation: Cognito User Pools handle sign-up/sign-in and social identity federation (Google, Facebook). Cognito Identity Pools then exchange user pool tokens for temporary AWS credentials scoped with IAM policies, enabling per-user DynamoDB access via fine-grained conditions.

scenario: A gaming application uses DynamoDB to store player profiles. Read latency averages 5ms, but the game requires sub-millisecond read latency for leaderboard queries during tournaments. How should the architecture be optimized?

options.text: Enable DynamoDB Auto Scaling to increase read capacity during tournaments
Add a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the table
Create a Global Secondary Index optimized for leaderboard queries
Switch from DynamoDB to Amazon ElastiCache Redis for all game data

explanation: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB. It reduces read latency from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, requiring minimal code changes. Auto Scaling adjusts capacity but doesn't reduce latency. GSIs improve query flexibility but not latency.

scenario: A VPC has public and private subnets. The security team wants to allow inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the public subnet but deny all other inbound traffic. They also want to log all denied traffic for forensic analysis. Which combination of controls should be used?

options.text: Configure security groups to allow HTTP/HTTPS and enable VPC Flow Logs
Configure NACLs to allow inbound HTTP/HTTPS and deny all else, combined with VPC Flow Logs set to capture REJECT traffic
Use AWS Network Firewall stateful rules with alert logging
Configure a web application firewall on each EC2 instance

explanation: NACLs provide subnet-level stateless filtering and can explicitly deny traffic. VPC Flow Logs with REJECT filter capture all denied network flows for forensic analysis. Security groups cannot explicitly deny traffic and don't log denials. Network Firewall is more complex than needed for simple port filtering.

scenario: A company needs to reduce cross-region data transfer costs between their application in us-east-1 and a disaster recovery site in eu-west-1. They transfer 10TB of database replication data monthly. Which approach helps reduce these costs?

options.text: Compress data before replication to reduce the volume of transferred bytes
Switch to S3 Transfer Acceleration for faster, cheaper cross-region transfers
Use VPC Peering which eliminates cross-region data transfer charges
Move both regions to the same geographic area to reduce transfer distance

explanation: Compressing data before cross-region transfer directly reduces the volume of bytes transferred, proportionally reducing data transfer costs. Cross-region transfer is charged per GB ($0.02/GB), so compressing 10TB by 60% saves approximately $120/month. S3 Transfer Acceleration adds cost, doesn't reduce it. VPC peering does NOT eliminate cross-region transfer charges.

scenario: A company needs to run lightweight request transformations (URL rewrites, header manipulation, A/B testing) at CloudFront edge locations with sub-millisecond execution time. Which compute option is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Lambda@Edge functions triggered by CloudFront events
CloudFront Functions for lightweight, short-running edge computations
An origin-side Lambda function behind API Gateway
A fleet of EC2 instances deployed in every AWS region

explanation: CloudFront Functions run at CloudFront edge locations with sub-millisecond startup time and support up to millions of requests per second. They're designed for lightweight transformations like URL rewrites, header manipulation, cache key normalization, and simple A/B testing. Lambda@Edge is more powerful but has higher latency and cost.

scenario: A startup is building a new serverless API backend. They expect highly variable traffic — from 10 requests per minute during off-hours to 10,000 per second during viral events. They want zero idle costs. Which architecture minimizes cost while handling scale?

options.text: EC2 Auto Scaling group with minimum capacity of 2 instances behind an ALB
API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB on-demand mode for a fully pay-per-use stack
ECS Fargate with minimum 2 running tasks and Application Auto Scaling
Elastic Beanstalk with a t3.small instance and Auto Scaling

explanation: API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB on-demand is fully serverless with no idle costs. You pay only per API call, per Lambda invocation (per 1ms), and per DynamoDB read/write request. During zero traffic, the cost is $0. All three services auto-scale to handle sudden bursts without pre-provisioning. EC2/ECS/Beanstalk all have minimum running costs.

scenario: A company runs a critical e-commerce database on Amazon RDS MySQL. They need the database to automatically failover to a standby replica in another Availability Zone with minimal data loss if the primary fails. Which RDS feature provides this?

options.text: RDS Read Replicas with manual promotion
RDS Multi-AZ deployment with synchronous standby replication
RDS cross-region read replica with asynchronous replication
RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ creates a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ. During a failure, RDS automatically promotes the standby to primary with no data loss and a typical failover time of 60-120 seconds. Read replicas use asynchronous replication and require manual promotion.

scenario: A company wants to design a fault-tolerant batch processing pipeline that can handle worker node failures without losing progress on long-running jobs. Which TWO design patterns should be applied? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use SQS to track individual work items and process them independently on worker instances
Implement checkpointing to S3 so workers can resume from the last saved state after restart
Run all batch processing on a single powerful instance to avoid coordination complexity
Store intermediate results in instance store volumes for maximum I/O performance
Use a synchronous request-response pattern between the scheduler and workers

explanation: SQS-based work distribution ensures that if a worker fails, the unprocessed message becomes visible again for another worker to pick up. Checkpointing to S3 allows workers to save progress and resume from the last checkpoint after a restart, avoiding reprocessing of completed work. Instance store volumes are lost when instances terminate.

scenario: An application needs to serve structured product catalog data with sub-millisecond read latency, automatic scaling, and no operational overhead for capacity planning. The access patterns are well-defined key-value lookups. Which database is BEST suited?

options.text: Amazon RDS MySQL with ElastiCache for caching
Amazon DynamoDB in on-demand capacity mode
Amazon DocumentDB for flexible schema queries
Amazon Neptune for relationship-heavy data traversals

explanation: DynamoDB in on-demand mode provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale with no capacity planning. It automatically scales read/write capacity based on traffic patterns. For well-defined key-value access patterns, DynamoDB is optimal. RDS with ElastiCache adds operational complexity. DocumentDB and Neptune are for different access patterns.

scenario: An application must securely store and automatically rotate database credentials every 30 days. Developers should retrieve credentials programmatically without hardcoding them. Which service is BEST suited?

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString parameters
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled
Store credentials in an encrypted S3 object and read at startup
AWS KMS to encrypt credentials embedded in the application configuration file

explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for managing secrets like database credentials, API keys, and tokens. It natively supports automatic rotation using Lambda functions, and provides an API for programmatic retrieval. Parameter Store SecureString can store secrets but lacks built-in rotation.
